title: hosted-api-peak-scaling-playbook-q3-2026
summary: Working capacity planning sheet for expected Q3 2026 hosted API peak patterns. Includes per-region peak projections (QPS & tokens/sec), GPU equivalence math, recommended reserve counts and operational playbook for maintaining headroom under multi-model mix.
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet consolidates recent traffic telemetry, forecast signals (sales, PLG adoption, and partner launches), and worst-case headroom targets to produce a recommended regional capacity posture for Hosted API in Q3 2026. Use for sizing reserved pools, pre-warm windows, and autoscaler guardrails.

High-level assumptions:
- Forecast horizon: July–September 2026 (Q3).
- Model mix (traffic-weighted): 60% chat-xl (slow tokens), 30% chat-l (mid), 10% embeddings/batch.
- Observed avg tokens per request (weighted): 700 tokens/request.
- 99th-percentile request size 95th percentile multiplier: x1.6 => plan with 1120 tokens/request for burst calc.
- Conversion: 1 H100 equiv = 2.1 A100 for our transformer mix; L40 ~1.7 A100-equivalent. Use H100-equivalent GPUs as canonical sizing unit.
- Target operational headroom: 30% steady-state buffer above forecasted 99p peaks; emergency burst capacity of additional 15% accessible within 2 minutes via burst pool (region or cross-region failover).

Raw telemetry snapshot (last 4 weeks, global):
- Mean sustained QPS: 420 QPS
- 95th QPS: 890 QPS
- Observed peak QPS (single-day spike): 1,420 QPS
- Mean tokens/sec global: ~294k tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec (single-day): ~1.0M tokens/sec

Regional projections (Q3 planning targets):
Table (plain):
Region | Forecast 99p QPS (Q3 peak) | Forecast 99p tokens/sec | Planned headroom target (+30%) tokens/sec | H100-equiv GPUs required (rounded) | Current reserved (H100-equiv)
us-west1 | 1,200 QPS | 840,000 t/s | 1,092,000 t/s | 48 | 36
us-east4 | 900 QPS | 630,000 t/s | 819,000 t/s | 36 | 28
eu-west1 | 600 QPS | 420,000 t/s | 546,000 t/s | 24 | 20
asia-southeast1 | 350 QPS | 245,000 t/s | 318,500 t/s | 14 | 10
Note: GPUs required computed from microbenchmarks: 1 H100-equiv sustains ~22,500 tokens/sec for our chat-xl mix at target latency SLO; values rounded up to nearest whole GPU.

Capacity arithmetic (example for us-west1):
- Forecast tokens/sec: 840k
- +30% headroom => 1,092k tokens/sec
- H100-equiv per-GPU sustained (SLO) = 22.5k t/s => 1,092k / 22.5k = 48.5 => round up to 48 GPUs (we recommend 50 to keep simple fault domains).

Cross-region guardrail recommendations:
- Maintain an async cross-region spill policy: if region falls below 15% spare capacity, route new requests to nearest region with available headroom (respecting data residency tags).
- Keep a global burst pool equal to 15% of total planned capacity (cold-startable within 2 min). This pool should be tiled across 3 regions to avoid single-region risk.

Autoscaler & orchestration settings (to apply by 2026-06):
- Min pool size = planned reserved GPUs per region (as table).
- Scale-up threshold: 80% sustained utilization for 30s OR short spikes crossing 95% for 10s trigger pre-warm actions.
- Pre-warm policy: on detection of sustained +20% QPS growth in 5m window, spin an additional pre-warm shard (warm in ~90s).
- Scale-down: only after 15m below 50% utilization and with a 5–10% scheduled cooldown to avoid oscillation.

Operational runbook (condensed):
- Incident detection: alert when regional spare capacity < 20% or tail latencies exceed SLO by >20% for 5m.
- Triage steps: check model mix changes (deploys), recent large-job injections (embeddings), and autoscaler logs.
- Quick mitigations: enable cross-region spill, increase burst pool if available, adjust batching window (reduce for latency-sensitive tenants), rollback recent model rollout if suspect.
- Postmortem: compute tokens/sec and QPS delta vs forecast, update the forecast model and headroom percentages accordingly.

Cost trade-offs and notes:
- Reserving +30% headroom increases monthly infra spend ~18% vs minimal-reserve baseline but reduces SLO incidents by estimated ~60% based on historical incident correlation.
- Consider adding quantization-first model variants for best-effort routes to reduce tokens/sec pressure; typically reduces per-token cost 18–25% but increases chance of quality regression. Use Canary + eval harness before routing traffic.

Open questions / action items:
- [A] Confirm H100 procurement timeline for Q3 (action: Marcus Li to confirm vendor lead times by 2026-03-15).
- [B] Validate per-GPU sustained t/s numbers for new model (chat-xl-v2) on L40 images (action: perf team run benchmark INF-612).
- [C] Decide on global burst pool funding (finance/ops) — proposal: cap at 15% of committed capacity.
- [D] Add data residency exceptions for EU customers before enabling cross-region spill (legal/ops).

Notes / context: this is intentionally a working artifact: numbers are conservative and biased toward reliability. Final reserved contracts should be signed only after vendor SKUs and prices are validated and after confirming on-prem/private customers who may absorb some steady usage.
